capability: Track 2 — corpus acquisition to frozen crystal (Stage 3, candidate extraction)
milestone: Track 2 Stage 3 — deterministic batched extraction over the admitted population
problem: Stage 3 extraction read a single bounded model context and reported success over the whole admitted population. At a 24,000-character budget with a 6,000-character per-row cap, at most FOUR evidence rows entered a pass; the packing loop then `break`ed, silently discarding every remaining row. A run over 32 admitted sources would compress four of them and return ok:true with no signal that 28 were never read. The operator's framing is sharper than 'truncation' and is the one to carry forward: partial evidence was processed as though the full population had been processed.
observedFailure: runConstitutionalDiscovery returned ok:true after reading at most four of the admitted evidence rows, with no field distinguishing a full read from a partial one.

The packing loop used `break`, so a small row that WOULD have fitted was dropped because a larger row earlier in the list did not — inclusion depended on fetch order rather than on whether the row fit.
Downstream readers (candidate review, the Track 2 programme projection) treated the resulting candidates as the corpus's output, because nothing in the result said otherwise.

A second instance of the same shape one level down: a row longer than 6,000 characters is capped, while one discovery_evidence row holds up to 200,000 characters — so up to 97% of a source could go unread while the candidate derived from it cited that source as its basis.
A first-draft canary for the completion guard passed with AND without the guard, because an adjacent condition already forced the same answer in the case it tested.
rootCauses: A capacity limit (model context) was implemented as silent truncation instead of as pagination or batching — the processor treated 'as much as fits' as 'the population'.
The processed set and the admitted population were never compared, so there was no mechanism by which a shortfall could be detected, let alone reported.
Completion was inferred from the absence of an error rather than from an accounting identity over the population.
The per-row cap and the per-batch budget were both applied as slices, with no distinction between 'this row was read' and 'this row was read in part'.

The first repair (break -> continue plus typed exclusions) made the result honest but left completeness unaddressed; honesty about a partial result is not the same property as processing the whole population.
resolution: Added services/invariants/batchedExtraction.ts: deterministic partitioning of the full admitted population into context-sized batches, reconciliation of every batch outcome, and global candidate dedup.
Partitioning sorts by evidence id BEFORE packing, so batches are a function of the SET rather than of fetch order, and a re-run over the same population yields identical batches.
A row that does not fit the current batch opens a new batch instead of ending the loop, so the order-dependence defect cannot recur.

Added the hard completion rule as executable arithmetic in extractionProgression: Stage 3 may report `complete` only when processed + explicitly excluded === admitted population, and never when the identity fails, whatever else looks healthy.
A failed batch quarantines only its own rows: the loop continues, its rows are recorded as an explicit exclusion with the failure named, and every other batch's candidates stand.

Global dedup runs AFTER reconciliation, never per batch, so the same statement surfaced independently by two batches survives once carrying the UNION of its evidence ids and the higher confidence — the convergence signal is preserved rather than discarded as noise.
Candidates are inserted ONCE, after dedup, so a statement found by two batches never produces two registry rows.
Row-level truncation is now disclosed as a typed exception naming how much of the row was read; the row still counts as processed because it did contribute.

Added services/invariants/discoveryEngine.ts::runBatchedConstitutionalDiscovery, composing those pure functions, with the per-batch model call factored out of the single-pass path so the two cannot drift.
rejectedApproaches: Raising the context budget. The limit is a real model constraint, not a tunable; a larger number would move the cliff rather than remove it, and would restore silent truncation the moment a corpus outgrew it.
Truncating each row further so more rows fit one pass. That processes a fragment of every source while reporting each as read — the same defect, applied more widely.

Treating a failed batch as a failed run. That reintroduces inside Stage 3 exactly the paralysis the exception-isolation ruling abolished at Stage 2: one timeout would discard an entire population's extraction.

Deduplicating within each batch. Two batches can independently surface the same invariant from different evidence; per-batch dedup cannot see that, so it would emit two near-identical registry rows and lose the convergence signal.
Inserting candidates per batch as they are produced. Simpler to write, but it persists duplicates before dedup can run and makes a partial run's rows indistinguishable from a complete one's.

Fixing row-level truncation in this change by splitting a row across batches. That is a distinct mechanism (reconciling partial readings of one document) and building it under cover of this work would be a speculative build; it is disclosed and recorded as outstanding instead.
Keeping the first-draft completion canary. It passed with and without the guard it claimed to protect, so it was replaced with a case where only the guard prevents a false `complete`.
